speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To investigate your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness, where exactly do you feel the weakness in your arms, and is your vision issue constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest, especially with vision changes on upward or downward gaze, strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction disorder. To confirm this, I need to know if you have ever experienced similar episodes before or if you have any history of myasthenia gravis or similar conditions.
